task_summary: Polish UX and UI using transferable editorial patterns from steipete.me while keeping Hugo and the current brand.
confirmed_assumptions: Keep Hugo, LoveIt, Lunr search, Lora reading typography, and the blue-pink brand palette.
Focus on icons, link states, clean post cards without tag clutter, and article heading hierarchy.
Do not reimplement the completed sticky header and command palette behavior.
Prefer reusable partials and scoped SCSS over additional inline styles or broad theme edits.
key_findings: The site has over 400 content pages but only about 26 posts, so it is a knowledge hub plus portfolio rather than a pure blog.
Post summaries currently expose tags and mixed metadata, increasing scan cost.
Heading level two is globally uppercase with wide tracking, which makes long-form articles feel like documentation sections.
Interactive icons and links do not share a single semantic or visual contract.
The stylesheet has high specificity and duplication, so changes must stay scoped to touched components.
suggested_approach: Implement a small editorial UX vertical slice: shared post-card partial without tags, consistent utility icon and link states, and article-scoped heading hierarchy. Verify all list contexts before replacing duplicated summary templates.
